en: (Blessing, Sequence of the Śrāddha Rite, and the Ritual for Bathing in the Ocean) || The Succession of Blessings || (F1a, 1st line) May there be well-being through the meaning of the *svasti* mantra! May there be well-being for this couple! Today, that which was performed by him has been perfectly accomplished. (2nd line)
On the ground strewn with cow dung within the mandala, upon large, long, and pointed plantain leaves,
a female attendant served a meal consisting of kāravallī held in the hands of an ascetic,
along with *praṭolī*, two kinds of *kūṣmāṇḍa*, *panasa*, and various leafy vegetables.

[He offered] a mass of various refined foods— such as clear, sweet rice cooked with milk (*sudhā*), excellent bean cakes (*māṣāpūpa*), *ṣaṣkulī* pastries, flour-cakes (*piṣṭaka*), and the finest items among those to be licked (*lehya*) and sucked (*coṣya*)— along with three kinds of soups, honey, curd, and various divine sandalwood pastes, jasmine flowers, and other fragrant substances.

Attaining great joy through the common offering of clusters of flowers, [he was honored] by those accompanied by groups of the virtuous— such as Vasiṣṭha, Parāśara, Pārāśarya, and others— who were gratified with yelā, lavaṅga, jasmine, kunda, *pracchamarīci*, betel nut, *nāgavallī*, and other offerings, and who bestowed various kinds of blessings according to their own respective inclinations.

May the Lord, the soul of all, Śrī Godāsameta Rājagopasvāmī— being well-pleased and highly gratified by the worship of Bharadvāja as performed by the Śrīvaiṣṇavas who preceded him, yet disregarded by their respective preferred [sects]— become the bestower of boons and the granter of the fulfillment of all desires; thus we pray to you.

May he, who is the manifestation from his own mouth of one skilled in the worship of Hayagrīva— who is accompanied by Lakṣmī, who is initiated into the seven threads beginning with the protection of those who have sought refuge, whose lotus feet shine with the splendor of the rays from the clusters of jewels set in the crowns of millions upon millions of gods and asuras— grant grace.

Having traversed the waves of the deep Ganges of knowledge— expanded by the mastery of all the difficult systems such as the *Dakṣiṇa-veda*, the *Veda*, the *Vedānta*, grammar, logic, and Mīmāṃsā— he mocks [his opponents] with a crown of dry arguments, which are sprouts of the flow of hypocrisy issuing forth unrestrainedly from his skill in disputation.
He whose enemies cry out in distress, who sports in crushing the skulls of learned men, whose feet shine with the beauty of the eighteen *purāṇas* as his bracelets,
who dwells in the sacred abode of Vasu— the most fortunate Padmapadmanātha—
[and] who possesses boundless majesty as one devoted to the tradition of the sovereign authority in determining the tenets of the venerable Lord Rāmānuja.

Through the grace of the venerable Vedāntadeśika— who is the most eminent among the great devotees of the Lord, who is the most excellent among the best of Brahmins, who is firmly established in Brahman, who possesses a profound discernment, and who is endowed with the glory of infinite auspicious qualities that are praiseworthy and unsurpassed—
may you, O great ones, obtain a long-lived son of noble character and many virtues. Thus [I pray].
May they favor this couple, who, like Janaki and the Lord of the Raghus, are ever accompanied by Arundhati;

who have rendered the assembly of all gods and brahmins joyful through the fragrance of the smoke from the oblation of handfuls of parched grain, made white by the series of divine and auspicious mantras uttered from their lotus-like faces.

May those two, whose lotus-like faces gaze upon one another while intent on various forms of mutual worship, and whose hearts— the lotuses of the entire assembly— are enchanted by Madhukamañjarī, who has broken into a gentle smile born of the modesty arising from that sight; may you, the great ones, deign to favor them thus.

"May this couple, whose minds are fixed upon the worship of the assembly of the ever-present saints and who possess firm devotion, be increased by the glances of the exceedingly compassionate side-long looks of Lakṣmī’s Beloved, who is well-pleased; may you great ones thus bestow your grace. May all the Śrīvaiṣṇavas residing in this auspicious hall—who are devoted to the six duties beginning with ritual bathing and the twilight prayers according to the Ṛg, Yajur, Sāma, and Atharva Vedas, and [who perform] the rites of conception (*ṛtusaṅgamana*) and impregnation (*garbhādhāna*)—"
[The rites] beginning with *puṃsavana*, *sīmanta*, *viṣṇubali*, *jātakarman*, *nāmakaraṇa*,
*annaprāśana*, *caula*, *upanayana*, *vedapārāyaṇa*, *vratibandha*, *vratodyāpana*, *samāvartana*, and *pāṇigrahaṇa*—
together with these eighteen auspicious acts (*śubhakarma*), as well as sacrificing for oneself, officiating at sacrifices for others, studying, teaching, giving gifts, and receiving gifts.

[He is] solely devoted to the exposition and investigation of the Drāviḍa Vedas numbering four thousand, as composed by Parāṅkuśa, Parakāla, and others; [he is] intent upon the six duties (*ṣaṭkarma*) such as the Agniṣṭoma, Agniṣṭomoktha, Ṣoḍaśī, Vājapeya, and so forth; [he is] devoted to the seven *pākayajñas*; [he is] one who has mastered the fourteen branches of knowledge (*caturdaśavidyā*), including the four Vedas beginning with the Aṅgas, the *Nyāya-vistara*, the *Purāṇas*, the *Dharmaśāstras*, and so on.

May there be auspiciousness for you, the illustrious ones who are devoted [to virtue], through your words of blessing; may these two spouses obtain eight sons and abundant wealth— may you, the great ones,
bestow this favor.
(For the *caula* ceremony, the asterism is *yetho*. Citrā, Śravaṇa, Hasta, Aśvinī, Puṣya, Āditya, and the Vaiṣṇava asterisms,
as well as Mṛgaśīrṣa and Puṣya, are honored for the rite of tonsure (*caula*).
Śvātī, Śatabhiṣaj, the three Rohiṇīs, and the three Uttarās—
these six are declared to be middling for the rite of shaving children.
One should avoid the remaining twelve asterisms for the rite of shaving.
